L250: Off-chip bandwidth is varied from DDR4-class levels to HBM-class levels to capture a wide performance spectrum. We assume that both NTT and SumCheck accelerators are integrated into an SoC with a shared DRAM PHY. To capture real-world scenarios, we test the problem sizes ($N\geq 2^{17}$) that approximate practical ZKP workloads such as Zcash, ZKP-based auctions, and private transaction protocols (【78†Daftardar et al., 2025a】).
L251: For hardware technology, we prototype compute engines and memory structures using commercial toolchains (【86†Mo et al., 2023b】; 【87†Mo and Reagen, 2023】). We use Catapult HLS 2024 to generate the RTL for Montgomery multipliers, constant-geometry NTT PEs and the fully pipelined SumCheck PE. The hardware assumes the 255-bit fixed primes used in (【78†Daftardar et al., 2025a】).
